chunks: And it was also narrated from Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The son's daughter is closer than the daughter's daughter.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two reports are not acted upon, because we have clarified that when there is a daughter of the trunk (son), neither the daughter's daughter nor the son's daughter inherits. Rather, each of them takes the place of the one through whom they are connected, if there is no one closer than them. As for the second report, which includes that the son's daughter is closer than the daughter's daughter, it is also not sound, because their degree is one, meaning that each of them connects through the one they connect with themselves, so their closeness is one. It is likely that these two reports came either as a mistake from the narrator, or they came to the place of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) because they agree with the belief of some of the Sunnis.

key_terms.لِلصُّلْبِ: Of the trunk/lineage (referring to the son)

ai.seo_question: How do Shia jurists determine the inheritance share of granddaughters when a son is present?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi notes that while the report aligns with Sunni jurisprudence, it is likely based on *taqiyya* (dissimulation) or narrator error, as Shia doctrine holds that both granddaughters share equal proximity by virtue of their respective parents. Consequently, they are treated as equal in rank when inheriting through representation, rather than one being strictly superior to the other.
